react_native_issues.issue: Console warning fires on chat load: 'Unexpected text node:         . A text node cannot be a child of a <View>.' — likely a stray whitespace/newline between JSX children (e.g. between two <View>s where a bare text-like space was inserted). Not blocking (messages render + send correctly) but noisy in dev console. Reference: /app/frontend/src/components/chat/MessageBubble.tsx and/or /app/frontend/app/chat/[id].tsx — check for a bare '{' ' '}' or a stray literal string between View children.

'"shadow*" style props are deprecated. Use "boxShadow".' warning still fires (carried over from iteration_5). Reference: /app/frontend/src/screens/ClientToday.tsx:543 (styles.fab uses shadowColor/shadowOpacity/shadowRadius/shadowOffset) plus any StyleSheet with shadow* on the coach dashboard.

'props.pointerEvents is deprecated. Use style.pointerEvents' warning fires on login screen — likely from a wrapping View or a Button component still passing pointerEvents as a prop instead of via style.

action_items: OPTIONAL: hunt down the stray whitespace text node that triggers 'A text node cannot be a child of a <View>' in the chat screen — quick fix is to remove any bare '{' ' '}' or inline literal between View siblings in MessageBubble.tsx / chat/[id].tsx.
OPTIONAL: migrate shadow* props to boxShadow in ClientToday.tsx (styles.fab) and any other component still using the deprecated shadow API.
OPTIONAL: find and fix the pointerEvents-as-prop usage on the login screen (should be style.pointerEvents).

Nice-to-have: consider adding testID to the coach-logo IMAGE fallback (currently only the branded logo has testID='coach-logo'), so tests can assert either brand or default logo is rendered on /welcome.
critical_code_review_comments: catalog.py — the DOMAIN/APPROACH/MODEL constants are the single source of truth and are referenced everywhere via DOMAIN_BY_KEY/APPROACH_BY_KEY/MODEL_BY_KEY dicts built at import time. If a domain key is renamed, ALL practice_profiles rows storing the old key silently drop that domain on next GET (filtered out via `[d for d in body.domains if d in DOMAIN_BY_KEY]`). That's the desired behaviour but worth a code comment.

routes_catalog.py::install_kit is idempotent by (coach_id, title) uniqueness on both checkin_templates and lead_forms. The idempotency is by-title not by-domain-key though — if a coach manually renames the Sleep check-in template, a subsequent install of 'sleep' will happily create a second copy. Consider tagging the install with a domain_key field so idempotency survives renames.
routes_catalog.py::install_kit only sets practice_installs on success — the practice_profiles.$addToSet:domain runs unconditionally, which is fine.

routes_uploads.py::COVER_PRESETS is 12 hard-coded Unsplash URLs. If any of those redirects/404s, the cover picker sheet will show broken thumbnails. Consider proxying through /api/files/{path} for stability — but that's a nice-to-have.
routes_misc.py::mark_welcomed is idempotent (unconditional $set:{welcomed:true}) — a client hitting the endpoint multiple times has no side effects.

server.py — routes_library is registered on line 96 BEFORE routes_uploads on line 97, keeping the iteration_5 fix in place. Verified with a fresh upload -> download round-trip in test_private_file_route_before_wildcard.

practice.tsx (frontend) — the do_not_do rule input clears after Add but the local state is only flushed to backend on Save; if the coach reloads before saving they lose typed rules. Consistent with how the whole form works, so probably by design.
welcome.tsx (frontend) — if /me/welcomed fails the client still gets routed into (tabs) (catch block), which is the right behaviour — a network hiccup should not permanently gate the app.

welcome.tsx — the coach-logo testID is only attached to the branded IMG when `coach.brand_logo` is truthy; if the coach hasn't set one, the app's default CC logo is shown WITHOUT testID. Fine for now; add testID to the fallback if you want a stable selector.

The Phase 6 catalog is a large static config (~500 lines of Python dicts). Consider moving it into a JSON asset shipped alongside the module so translators/copywriters can edit without touching Python. Not urgent.
